title: My journey with DesignUp
summary: How four years of volunteering at DesignUp, from photos to motion design and 3D, shaped me as a person and as a Designer.

items.text: [DesignUp](https://designup.io/) is a community and conference for product creators, designers, makers and technology leaders across India and Southeast Asia. It began in Bengaluru and grew through large conferences and smaller events across Indian cities and Singapore, bringing practitioners together to share their work, ideas and experience.

body.markdown: Some of the best things in my life happened because I was lucky enough to be in the right room, with the right people, at the right time. DesignUp was one of them. This is the story of how it shaped me, as a person and as a Designer, and a chance to share the work I was fortunate to create along the way.

Back in 2015, I was leading the Design team at Belong. Through work, I was introduced to [Jay Dutta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jaydutta/), and JD soon became someone I'd go to for all sorts of guidance: managing a team, hiring, my own growth as a Designer etc. JD used to give talks and organise small Design events in Bengaluru. I was curious and ambitious, so I'd attend as many as I could and help out wherever I could.
In 2016, when JD first shared his plan for DesignUp, I was more than excited to be part of it. Little did I know how much it was going to change me, both as a person and as a Designer.

Summer of 2016, we frequented a coffee shop in Koramangala. JD would tease the idea of a Design conference we would spend hours discussing details and sharing opinions.  He was looking for people who constantly shows up. Then it was decided, we are going to have the first DesignUp conference.

It was going to be a small event with just 200 people at a small venue in Church street, Bengaluru. We got all excited and the bunch of volunteers got together and starting preparing and planning the event. I was figuring a way to be useful and the one thing I had was a basic DSLR, and I offered to take photographs at the event.

body.caption: Meticulous planning for seamless entry, DUP2016

body.markdown: This was my first conference experience of any kind. The excitement, the hustle, and the energy, both while preparing and during to the event, was intoxicating. The talks, the interactions, the magic show, and the afterparty are all stuff that I fondly remember to this day.

It was at DesignUp 2016 that I saw Ranganath Krishnamani's work, which left me fascinated, inspired and wanting to do more. This became a theme for me, every DesignUp would inspire a changes me in a way that would define the direction of my future.

By DesignUp 2017, I had skilledUp, and I convinced JD for the budget to rent a Panasonic GH5, my dream video camera at the time. Here are the videos and photos I covered at the event. That year, I was introduced to Lucky's work. All the speaker intro animations were made by Lucky, and I was so inspired and motivated that I knew this was what I wanted to chase next.

body.markdown: Then came DesignUp 2018, and I signed up to do the motion graphics for the event without ever having used After Effects. "Excited accountability" is what I call it. I was excited, and driven by the desire to impress. What followed was the most intense month of learning and creating in my life, with more than 70 hours in After Effects. Here's what came out of it.

body.markdown: That year, JD also approved the budget to rent two cameras, multiple lenses and a gimbal, and I had a field day with the new toys. Looking back, I'm grateful he kept trusting me with a little more every year. Here's what I made with them.

body.markdown: We organized a bunch of single day events across multiple cities in India, Bengaluru, Pune, Chennai and Hyderabad. I went to cover each of these events.

body.markdown: 2018 was also the year DesignUp went international, and I was lucky enough to go along to Singapore.

Then it was time for DesignUp 2019, which meant a new challenge and another stepUp. This time, my fascination was 3D: mograph, textures, materials and simulations. I took on the task, and here's what came out of it.

By now, I had met so many leaders and great Designers. Year after year, I had been lucky to be surrounded by some of the best people in the industry. When you are constantly in the company of brilliant people, you can't help but grow. And it happened at a key moment in my career, when I was still growing, still being moulded, and still defining the kind of professional I wanted to be.

body.text: I went to DesignUp to help. I came back with far more than I could ever give.

body.markdown: Volunteering for DesignUp was one of the best things that happened in my career. Thank to JD and the entire DesignUp team, for letting me be a part of it.
